stem: A market where goods are bought and sold in large quantities, usually by traders rather than final consumers, is a:
solution: In a wholesale market, goods are bought and sold in bulk; wholesalers then supply retailers.

stem: A market that is set up on a particular day of the week and then packs up is called a:
solution: A weekly market or 'haat' is held on a fixed day each week; traders set up temporary stalls and move on.

stem: A person who buys goods in bulk from producers and sells them to retailers is called a:
solution: A wholesaler buys large quantities from producers and sells to retail shopkeepers, forming a link in the market chain.

stem: Which of the following is an advantage of a weekly market?
options: Goods are always more expensive than in shops
Many things are available cheaply in one place, and sellers save on shop rent
solution: Weekly markets offer a variety of goods at low prices in one place, and traders avoid the cost of maintaining a permanent shop.

stem: The usual chain through which goods reach us is:
solution: Goods typically move from the producer to a wholesaler, then to a retailer, and finally to the consumer.

stem: Buying goods through websites and apps, with home delivery, is an example of a(n):
solution: Online markets let buyers and sellers transact over the internet, with goods delivered to the buyer.

stem: A shop that sells goods in small quantities directly to consumers is engaged in:
solution: Retail trade involves selling goods in small quantities directly to the final consumers.

stem: A 'market' in economics refers to:
options: Any arrangement that enables buyers and sellers to exchange goods and services
A place where only vegetables are sold
solution: In ECONOMICS, a MARKET is ANY ARRANGEMENT that enables BUYERS and SELLERS to EXCHANGE goods and services — not necessarily a physical building. So option 2 is correct.

stem: The two essential participants in any market are:
solution: Every MARKET needs two essential participants: BUYERS (who demand goods) and SELLERS (who supply them). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The amount of a good that consumers are willing and able to buy at a given price is called:
solution: DEMAND is the amount of a good that CONSUMERS are WILLING and ABLE to BUY at a given PRICE. So option 2 is correct.

stem: The amount of a good that sellers are willing to offer for sale at a given price is called:
solution: SUPPLY is the amount of a good that SELLERS are WILLING to OFFER for sale at a given PRICE. So option 2 is correct.

stem: Generally, when the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded by consumers tends to:
solution: Generally, when PRICE RISES, the quantity DEMANDED tends to FALL, as goods become less affordable — the law of demand. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): In a market, prices are influenced by demand and supply. Reason (R): When demand is high and supply is low, prices tend to rise. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — prices are influenced by demand and supply. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: when DEMAND is HIGH and SUPPLY is LOW, PRICES tend to RISE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A 'wholesaler' is a trader who:
options: Buys goods in large quantities and sells to retailers
solution: A WHOLESALER buys goods in LARGE QUANTITIES from producers and sells them to RETAILERS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Match List-I with List-II: P. Producer Q. Wholesaler R. Retailer S. Consumer | 1. Buys in bulk, sells to retailers 2. Makes/grows the goods 3. Final user of the good 4. Sells small quantities to buyers
solution: Producer → makes/grows goods (P-2); Wholesaler → buys in bulk, sells to retailers (Q-1); Retailer → sells small quantities (R-4); Consumer → final user (S-3). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The person who finally uses or consumes a good is the:
solution: The CONSUMER is the person who finally USES or CONSUMES a good — the last link in the market chain. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a service (rather than a good) traded in markets?
solution: A HAIRCUT is a SERVICE (an activity performed for others), whereas rice, shoes and phones are GOODS (physical products). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The price at which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied is called the:
solution: The price at which quantity DEMANDED EQUALS quantity SUPPLIED is the EQUILIBRIUM or MARKET price. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the following statements: 1. Competition among sellers can keep prices lower. 2. If there is only one seller, that seller may charge higher prices. Which is/are correct?
solution: BOTH are correct: COMPETITION among sellers keeps prices LOWER (1), while a SINGLE seller (monopoly) may charge HIGHER prices (2). So option 1 is correct.

stem: When many sellers compete to sell similar goods, buyers generally benefit through:
solution: COMPETITION among many sellers generally benefits buyers through LOWER PRICES and MORE CHOICE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A market with only one seller of a good is called a:
solution: A market with only ONE SELLER of a good is a MONOPOLY, where that seller has great control over price. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): Prices of vegetables may fall when there is a bumper (very large) harvest. Reason (R): A large harvest increases supply, and higher supply with the same demand pushes prices down. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — a bumper harvest lowers vegetable prices. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: a LARGE HARVEST raises SUPPLY, and higher supply with the same demand PUSHES PRICES DOWN. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A weekly market and a shopping mall are both markets, but they differ in:
options: Their location, timing, prices, and the customers they serve
solution: A WEEKLY MARKET and a MALL differ in LOCATION, TIMING, PRICES, and the CUSTOMERS they serve, though both are markets. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The chapter shows that a single product can pass through many hands, which means:
options: Several traders and steps connect the producer to the final consumer
solution: A product passing through many hands means SEVERAL TRADERS and STEPS (wholesalers, retailers, transporters) CONNECT the PRODUCER to the final CONSUMER. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Demand — willingness to buy 2. Supply — willingness to sell 3. Retailer — sells to consumers. How many are correctly matched?
solution: ALL THREE match: DEMAND → willingness to buy; SUPPLY → willingness to sell; RETAILER → sells to consumers. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Online markets have grown because they:
options: Let people buy and sell from a distance conveniently, with home delivery
solution: ONLINE MARKETS have grown because they let people BUY and SELL from a DISTANCE CONVENIENTLY, with HOME DELIVERY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A 'brand' on a product mainly serves to:
options: Identify the maker and influence buyers' choices
solution: A BRAND IDENTIFIES the MAKER and INFLUENCES buyers' CHOICES, often through advertising and reputation. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Advertising affects markets mainly by:
options: Influencing consumers' demand and choices for products
solution: ADVERTISING affects markets by INFLUENCING consumers' DEMAND and CHOICES for products. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why might the same good cost more in a mall than in a weekly market?
options: Malls have higher overhead costs (rent, staff, electricity) reflected in prices
solution: The same good may cost MORE in a MALL because malls have HIGHER OVERHEAD costs (RENT, STAFF, ELECTRICITY) reflected in higher PRICES. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The market chain generally adds to a product's final price because:
options: Each trader adds costs and a profit margin
Traders reduce the price at each step
solution: The MARKET CHAIN ADDS to the final price because EACH TRADER adds their COSTS and a PROFIT MARGIN. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about access to markets?
options: People's ability to buy depends on their income, so access is unequal
solution: ACCESS to markets is UNEQUAL because people's ability to BUY depends on their INCOME. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The main role of markets in an economy is to:
options: Connect producers and consumers and allow the exchange of goods and services
solution: The MAIN ROLE of MARKETS is to CONNECT producers and consumers and ENABLE the EXCHANGE of goods and services. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A 'consumer' benefits from a competitive market mainly through:
options: Better quality, lower prices, and greater choice
solution: In a COMPETITIVE market, a CONSUMER benefits from BETTER QUALITY, LOWER PRICES, and GREATER CHOICE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: If demand for a festival item like lamps rises sharply before a festival, its price is likely to:
solution: If DEMAND for festival lamps RISES sharply while supply is limited, the PRICE is likely to RISE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which statement best describes the relationship between markets and daily life?
options: Almost all goods and services we use reach us through markets
Markets have no effect on daily life
We produce everything we use ourselves
Markets exist only for the rich
solution: ALMOST ALL the GOODS and SERVICES we use reach us through MARKETS, making markets central to daily life. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A 'producer' in the market is someone who:
options: Makes or grows goods (or provides services) to be sold
solution: A PRODUCER MAKES or GROWS goods (or provides services) to be SOLD in the market. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the following statements: 1. Buyers prefer lower prices. 2. Sellers prefer higher prices. The market price is often a balance between the two. Which is/are correct?
options: Both 1 and 2 with a balancing price
solution: BOTH are correct and the market price often BALANCES them: BUYERS prefer LOWER prices, SELLERS prefer HIGHER prices, and the MARKET PRICE settles in between through demand and supply. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The chapter helps us understand markets so that we can:
options: Make informed choices as buyers and understand how prices and trade work
solution: Understanding markets helps us MAKE INFORMED CHOICES as BUYERS and understand how PRICES and TRADE work. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): Middlemen (wholesalers and retailers) play a useful role in markets. Reason (R): They help move goods from producers to widely spread consumers efficiently. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — middlemen play a useful role. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: they help MOVE goods from PRODUCERS to widely SPREAD CONSUMERS EFFICIENTLY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A shopkeeper's 'profit' is:
options: The amount left after subtracting costs from the selling price
solution: PROFIT is the amount LEFT after SUBTRACTING COSTS (buying price, rent, etc.) from the SELLING PRICE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is an example of the wholesale stage in the market chain?
options: A trader buying 100 sacks of onions from farmers to sell to shops
A family buying 1 kg of onions
A cook using onions in a dish
solution: A trader buying 100 SACKS of onions from farmers to sell to SHOPS is the WHOLESALE stage — bulk buying and selling to retailers. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why do prices of some goods vary from place to place?
options: Differences in transport costs, local demand and supply, and taxes
solution: PRICES vary across places due to differences in TRANSPORT COSTS, local DEMAND and SUPPLY, and TAXES. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A market where goods are sold in very large quantities to traders rather than to individual consumers is a:
solution: A WHOLESALE MARKET sells goods in very LARGE QUANTITIES to TRADERS, not to individual consumers. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The concept of 'demand and supply' is important because together they help determine:
options: The price of a good in the market
solution: DEMAND and SUPPLY together help DETERMINE the PRICE of a good in the market. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following best captures how a modern market differs from simple barter?
options: It uses money and involves chains of producers, traders and consumers with prices set by demand and supply
solution: A MODERN MARKET uses MONEY and involves CHAINS of producers, traders, and consumers, with PRICES set by DEMAND and SUPPLY — unlike simple barter. So option 1 is correct.

stem: When supply of a good increases greatly while demand stays the same, the price tends to:
solution: When SUPPLY INCREASES greatly while DEMAND stays the same, the PRICE tends to FALL. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A key reason to study 'Understanding Markets' is to see that markets are:
options: An organised system connecting production and consumption, shaped by prices, demand and supply
solution: Studying markets shows they are an ORGANISED SYSTEM connecting PRODUCTION and CONSUMPTION, shaped by PRICES, DEMAND, and SUPPLY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A consumer comparing prices and quality before buying is practising:
solution: Comparing PRICES and QUALITY before buying is INFORMED DECISION-MAKING as a consumer in the market. So option 1 is correct.

stem: If a new seller enters a market that had only one seller, consumers are likely to gain because:
options: Competition may lower prices and improve choice and quality
solution: When a NEW SELLER enters a one-seller market, COMPETITION may LOWER PRICES and improve CHOICE and QUALITY for consumers. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Understanding Markets' is that:
options: Markets are arrangements where buyers and sellers exchange goods and services; prices are shaped by demand and supply and by competition; goods reach consumers through a chain of producers, wholesalers and retailers (and increasingly online); understanding how markets work helps us make informed choices, though access to markets remains unequal because it depends on income
solution: The OVERALL MESSAGE is that MARKETS are arrangements where BUYERS and SELLERS EXCHANGE goods and services; PRICES are shaped by DEMAND and SUPPLY and by COMPETITION; goods reach consumers through a CHAIN of PRODUCERS, WHOLESALERS, and RETAILERS (and increasingly ONLINE); understanding markets helps us make INFORMED CHOICES, though ACCESS remains UNEQUAL because it depends on INCOME. So option 2 is correct.
